stumbles.quote: 42/43 violations in every form, even with no directive
stumbles.why: Unclear what this ratio means: 42 of 43 prompts violated? Also 'every form' (of CAPS? of directive?) and 'violations' of what rule are never defined.
The directive isn't described. It's unclear what the model was told to do or avoid, and if there was no directive, what counts as a violation.

stumbles.quote: Naming a forbidden word raised it ~2.5 log-odds.
stumbles.why: 'It' is ambiguous (compliance or violation rate?). 'Raised' is also unclear in direction, and the baseline is missing. It seems to conflict with the claim that violations are already near-ceiling at 42/43.
Unexplained name. A reader can guess it's a 321M-parameter model but not what it is or who made it.

stumbles.quote: Its 22,100 training docs hold one caps instruction
stumbles.why: 'Its' presumably refers to Baguettotron's training corpus, but this is never stated. The link between this fact and the compliance result is left implicit.

point: A tiny 321M model ignored forbidden-word instructions nearly always regardless of CAPS emphasis, only naming the word shifted behavior, and that may be because its training data contains almost no caps instructions.
